models.purpose: Score a monthly water level by the five stakeholder interests it serves.
models.summary: Five benefit terms are written and then combined. Coastal protection cost is a step function of the rise above the historical mean, scaled by shoreline length and population density. Hydropower revenue follows the change in head across three plants. Leisure satisfaction is the standard deviation of the monthly level. Shipping revenue is the flow divided by the square root of the head difference, normalized by the historical head. The ecological term is the ratio of the high-low range to its historical range. AHP weights the five, three of them negative, and the fitness is the absolute value of the weighted sum.

models.section: 3.1 Hydrodynamic Model of the Lake Chain
models.purpose: Simulate how a change at one lake moves downstream through the chain.
models.summary: The lakes are a chain from Superior to the Atlantic. The level of each lake changes at the net inflow divided by its area. The flow between lakes is a Manning-Strickler relation rewritten on the head difference, the width and a friction term, and the Huron-Erie reach adds a time lag because Lake St. Clair is treated as a river. The inflow of a lake is the outflow of the lake above plus rain minus evaporation.

models.purpose: Hold the five lakes at their target levels using the two dams.
models.summary: The classical controller is a PID. The upstream dam normally runs proportional to the Lake Superior error and switches to proportional-integral once the accumulated error on Huron and Michigan passes a threshold. The downstream dam releases the minimum of its maximum and the estimated net inflow when an upstream lake passes a flood threshold, and otherwise runs proportional-integral. A prediction module rolls the chain forward 200 hours and retunes the two downstream gains by gradient descent on the summed squared level error.
